label: Lithium iron phosphate (LiFePO4) / graphite
ocv_source: Prada et al. 2013, J. Electrochem. Soc. 160(4), A616 (A123 LFP/graphite cell model); LFP OCP Afshar 2017, graphite OCP Chen 2020; full-cell curve computed from the PyBaMM 'Prada2013' parameter set (2.30 Ah vs 2.3 Ah rated)
resistance_source: Activation energy fitted to the A123 ANR26650M1-B datasheet (MD100113-02, 2.5C discharge): voltage drop x2.5 at 0 °C and x5 at -15 °C vs 23 °C, both = 27 kJ/mol. Voltage drop at 1C/25 °C: assumption for a complete EV pack incl. interconnects
thermal_source: Pack: BYD Han Blade pack ≈ 140 Wh/kg (vendor figure; Tesla's LFP Model 3 pack ≈ 125 Wh/kg). Cells: measured LFP pouch and prismatic cells 1.0–1.15 J/(g·K) (batterydesign.net summary of measurements)
ageing_source: Shape: NREL BLAST-Lite model of a 250 Ah prismatic LFP/graphite cell (NREL 2023, J. Energy Storage 73, 109042): calendar fade ∝ time^0.526, cycle fade ∝ cycles^0.828. Activation energy 30 kJ/mol: inside the range of the lab fits (about 16–67 kJ/mol across the NREL BLAST-Lite cell models) and in line with Geotab 2026 (EVs in hot climates fade about 0.4 %/year faster than in mild ones). Size: fitted to Tesla Model 3 LFP (CATL) packs in Sweden, 93.3 % after more than 100,000 km (Carla / AVILOO tests 2022–2026); see degradation_measurements.csv. Calendar ageing vs. state of charge (calendar_soc.csv, used for the time parked above 80 %): the anode-potential term of the same BLAST-Lite model, graphite potential vs. charge from Safari & Delacourt 2011 (J. Electrochem. Soc. 158(5), A562), at 25 °C
rated_cycles_note: Your research (EV Calculations.ods, Car Details). For comparison, NREL's large-format lab cell (250 Ah, BLAST-Lite) reaches 80 % after about 3,700 full cycles at C/2 and 25 °C

label: Lithium nickel manganese cobalt oxide (NMC811) / graphite
ocv_source: Chen et al. 2020, J. Electrochem. Soc. 167, 080534 (LG M50 NMC811/graphite-SiOx cell); full-cell curve computed from the PyBaMM 'Chen2020' parameter set (5.10 Ah vs 5.0 Ah rated)
resistance_source: Kubal et al. 2022, J. Power Sources 543, 231864 (Argonne National Laboratory, OSTI 1962091): apparent activation energy of the area-specific impedance 27-31 kJ/mol for NMC532/622/811 full cells, -20..40 °C. Voltage drop at 1C/25 °C: assumption for a complete EV pack incl. interconnects
thermal_source: Pack: NMC packs ≈ 160–180 Wh/kg (vendor figures). Cells: measured NMC cells 0.96–1.04 J/(g·K) (batterydesign.net summary of measurements)
ageing_source: Shape: NREL BLAST-Lite model of a 75 Ah automotive NMC/graphite pouch cell (NREL 2023, J. Energy Storage 73, 109042): calendar fade ∝ time^0.578, cycle fade ∝ cycles^1.11. Activation energy 30 kJ/mol: inside the range of the lab fits (about 16–67 kJ/mol across the NREL BLAST-Lite cell models) and in line with Geotab 2026 (EVs in hot climates fade about 0.4 %/year faster than in mild ones). Size: fitted to fleet data (Tesla Model 3 NMC in Sweden, Tesla Model 3/Y after 200,000 miles, Geotab 2026 average 2.3 %/year); see degradation_measurements.csv. Calendar ageing vs. state of charge (calendar_soc.csv, used for the time parked above 80 %): the anode-potential term of the same BLAST-Lite model, graphite potential vs. charge from Safari & Delacourt 2011 (J. Electrochem. Soc. 158(5), A562), at 25 °C
rated_cycles_note: Your research (EV Calculations.ods, Car Details). For comparison, NREL's large-format lab cell (75 Ah, a high-power cell, BLAST-Lite) reaches 80 % after about 3,350 full cycles at C/2 and 25 °C
